chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muhammad ibn Humran, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

'Indeed, God — Mighty and Majestic — whenever He intends good for a servant, imprints a spot of divine light in his heart, and opens the channels of hearing of his heart, and assigns an angel with him who guides him aright. And whenever He intends evil for a servant, He imprints a black spot in his heart, closes the channels of hearing of his heart, and assigns a devil with him who leads him astray.'

Then he recited this verse: 'So whoever God wills to guide, He expands his chest for Islam; and whoever He wills to lead astray, He makes his chest narrow and straitened, as though he were ascending into the sky.' [6:125]

key_terms.عزّ وجلّ: Mighty and Majestic — an honorific for God denoting His power and greatness
key_terms.مسامع القلب: Channels/hearings of the heart — the spiritual faculties by which the heart perceives divine realities
key_terms.نكتة سوداء: A black spot — signifying spiritual darkness and hardness of heart in one whom God does not guide
key_terms.نكتة من نور: A spot/imprint of divine light — signifying spiritual illumination and receptivity to truth placed in the heart
key_terms.يسدده: To guide aright, to keep on the straight path — said of the angel's role in directing the guided person

ai.seo_question: How does God guide or mislead servants according to Imam Sadiq in al-Kafi?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) explains the divine mechanism of guidance and misguidance. When God intends good for a person, He illuminates their heart with divine light and opens their spiritual perception, appointing an angel to direct them. When He intends ill, He darkens their heart, seals their spiritual hearing, and appoints a devil to mislead them. The Imam then cites Quran 6:125, which uses the vivid metaphor of a chest expanded for receptivity to truth versus one contracted as if climbing to the sky — a physical impossibility representing spiritual incapacity. This hadith situates divine guidance within a framework of God's will while affirming the real, experiential difference between states of receptivity and hardness of heart.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim Bin Hashim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muhammad Bin Humran, from Suleyman Bin Khalid, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic, whenever He<sup>azwj</sup> Intends good with a servant, Imprints a spot of ‘Noor’ (The Invisible Light) into his heart, and Opens the hearing of his heart, and Allocates and Angel with him who would guide him. And when He<sup>azwj</sup> intends evil with a servant, Imprints a black spot into his hear and Shuts the hearings of his heart, and Allocate a Satan<sup>la</sup> with him to stray him’.

Then he recited this Verse [6:125] Therefore (for) whomsoever Allah Intends that He would Guide him aright, He Expands his chest for Islam, and (for) whomsoever He Intends that He should Let him to err, He makes his chest straitened and narrow as though he were ascending to the sky’.
